question: Are there exactly 13 prime numbers between 4,083 and 4,182 inclusive?

claims.text: There are exactly 12 primes between 4083 and 4182, not 13.
Any composite in the range has a prime factor at most about 64.7, so testing primes up to 61 suffices.
Prime density near 4000 is about 1 in 8.3, so about 12 primes are expected in a 100-number window.
The heuristic expectation makes 13 primes plausible, and nothing structural rules it out.
Trial division of every candidate yields exactly 12 primes.
4087 equals 61 times 67, so it is composite.
4097 equals 17 times 241, so it is composite.
4181 equals 37 times 113, so it is composite.
The plausibility argument for 13 is only heuristic, while the explicit enumeration is definitive.
